analysis.title: Smart Money Is Buying Small Caps
key_insights: The Russell 2000 is trading on a major trend line near the 200-day moving average. The last time it undershot the 200-day, it proved a good buying opportunity.

Per Goldman's Robert Quinn, non-dealers bought about $3bn of Russell 2000 futures between September 1 and 22. Asset managers accounted for $2.2bn, with smaller amounts from hedge funds and non-reportables.

Non-dealer positioning in Russell futures entered September at a multi-year low, so the buying started from a washed-out base. The open question is whether it marks a reversal or is overwhelmed by deteriorating credit.

The 30-year yield rose from 5.25% to 5.69% in seven sessions, and bond Daily Sentiment fell to 10%. BTIG, which has been looking for higher yields for months, now sees increasing risk of a sharp tactical reversal lower.
A reversal lower in the 10-year yield could feed quickly into a bid for small caps, given how closely small caps have tracked rates.
BTIG argues lower yields may not rescue tech. They could instead trigger a reversal in QQQ/IWM and similar relationships, with better breadth and stronger small caps while QQQ and Mag 7 move lower.
RVX (small-cap vol) has risen only modestly. Given the size of the sell-off, it was expected to react much more strongly relative to VXN, so the vol market shows little panic.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The rate move is stretched. BTIG sees increasing risk of a sharp tactical reversal lower, which would support small caps.
Sentiment on bonds has collapsed, a contrarian signal that supports a reversal lower in yields.

trade_ideas.description: Long small caps (Russell 2000 / IWM) for a reversal off the 200-day moving average, contingent on yields reversing lower
trade_ideas.rationale: The Russell sits on major trend line support, positioning is washed out, professionals are buying, and small-cap vol is contained.
trade_ideas.risk: Deteriorating credit could overwhelm the contrarian buying.

Lower yields may not help tech, and QQQ and Mag 7 could fall as small caps rally.
